issues.problem: 稿件把“立刻出发”写成无条件的原计划。证据显示，这只是按期登陆前提下的安排；原文还写了备选方案：登陆太晚就越冬、布置补给站，到1915年尽早出发。中英文都截去了这个条件。

evidence.quote: Should this be done, the Transcontinental party will set out on their 1800-mile journey at once

Should the landing be made too late in the season, the party will go into winter quarters, lay out depots during the autumn and the following spring, and as early as possible in 1915 set out on the journey.

issues.proposed: zh 改为：原计划要宏大得多：若能按时登陆，横穿队伍就立刻出发，走1800英里，希望五个月内穿越极点、抵达罗斯海基地；若登陆太晚，就先越冬、布置补给站，1915年尽早出发。en 同步补上 "Should the landing be made too late in the season..." 这一备选。
issues.rationale: 中英文都补上了“按时登陆”这个前提，并写入登陆太晚时的备选：先越冬，在秋季和次年春季布置补给站，1915年尽早出发。英文另起一句转述备选部分，ev 增加 S-E23。

issues.problem: 截断造成误导。海洋营所等待的第二次尝试实际做了：行军七天，直线只走了七英里半，食物只够四十二天，才不得不再次扎营，之后才有耐心营。稿件只写“后来他们又换了营地”，读者会以为海洋营的等待直接通向耐心营。

evidence.quote: We had been on the march for seven days
We had marched seven and a half miles in a direct line and at this rate it would take us over three hundred days to reach the land away to the west.
As we only had food for forty-two days there was no alternative, therefore, but to camp once more on the floe
Our new home, which we were to occupy for nearly three and a half months

issues.proposed: zh 改为：后来他们真的做了第二次尝试，行军七天，直线只前进七英里半；照这个速度要三百多天才能到西边的陆地，而食物只够四十二天，只好再次在浮冰上扎营，这就是耐心营，他们在那里住了将近三个半月。en 同步修改。
issues.rationale: 中英文都补出第二次尝试及其失败：行军七天，直线只前进七英里半，照此速度要三百多天才能到陆地，而食物只够四十二天，于是再次扎营，这才有了耐心营。ev 增加 S-E21。

issues.problem: 这一解读的前提与证据矛盾。稿件说海洋营的不同在于“这一次他把等待写成了一个计划”。但行军开始前，他已经写下“在最近的厚浮冰上扎营、等浮冰外漂到开阔水面”这个方案，当时因士气等心理原因否决，选择先走。海洋营是回到先前否决过的方案，不是第一次把等待写成计划。

evidence.quote: camp on the nearest heavy floe, scour the neighbouring pack for penguins and seals, and await the outward drift of the pack to open and navigable water.
Yet I feel sure that it is the right thing to attempt a march
There is a psychological aspect to the question also.

issues.proposed: 保留“一种解释是”的标注，把“海洋营的不同在于，这一次他把等待写成了一个计划”改为：行军前他其实已写下扎营等待的方案，并因心理原因否决；海洋营是在四天苦干之后回到这个方案，并加上了附近可能开出水道、可以划船去找陆地的指望。en 同步修改。
issues.rationale: 删去“这一次他把等待写成了一个计划”这一前提。改为：行军前他已写下扎营等待外漂的方案，因确信应先尝试行军并考虑到心理层面而否决；海洋营是四天苦干后回到这个方案，再加上附近可能开出水道的指望。仍标为作者推断，ev 增加 S-E19。

edits.before: The plan he began with was far grander: "the Transcontinental party will set out on their 1800-mile journey at once," he wrote, "in the hope of accomplishing the march across the Pole and reaching the Ross Sea base in five months." Once the ice had crushed the ship, the task became something else entirely: get the whole party onto land.
edits.after: The plan he began with was far grander. If the landing was made in time, "the Transcontinental party will set out on their 1800-mile journey at once," he wrote, "in the hope of accomplishing the march across the Pole and reaching the Ross Sea base in five months." Should the landing be made too late in the season, the party would go into winter quarters, lay out depots during the autumn and the following spring, and set out as early as possible in 1915. Once the ice had crushed the ship, the task became something else entirely: get the whole party onto land.

edits.after: 后来他们真的做了第二次尝试：行军七天，直线只前进了七英里半；照这个速度，要三百多天才能到西边的陆地，而食物只够四十二天，只好再次在浮冰上扎营。新的营地叫耐心营，他们在那里住了将近三个半月。

edits.before: Later they moved camp again, to a place they called Patience Camp, and lived there for nearly three and a half months.
edits.after: Later they did make that second attempt. They marched for seven days and gained seven and a half miles in a direct line; at that rate it would take over three hundred days to reach the land to the west, and they had food for only forty-two days. So they camped once more on the floe. They called the new camp Patience Camp and lived there for nearly three and a half months.

edits.before: 一种解释是（作者推断），海洋营不是他第一次决定停下。行军第二天早上，雪大得看不清路，他就决定不拔营；天晴一些后探到一块好走的浮冰，午饭后又继续走。两次决定都在衡量眼前的路还能不能走下去。海洋营的不同在于，这一次他把等待写成了一个计划：营地选在更结实的浮冰上，理由里挂着一个具体的指望——附近可能开出水道，那时可以划船去找陆地——等条件更有利，再做第二次尝试。

edits.before: A second reading, and it is the author's, concerns the standard behind the choices. The sovereigns were thrown away and the photographs were kept, and he gives no reason in these passages; the fly-leaf was torn out, and the passage does not say what became of it. The author's guess is that on the ice neither the gold coins nor the photographs could buy anything, yet the photographs were kept. Perhaps the limit screened only for weight; perhaps it was personal preference. Both go beyond what he wrote.
edits.after: A second reading, and it is the author's, concerns the standard behind the choices. The sovereigns were thrown away and the photographs were kept, and he did give his reasons. He admits he rather grudged the two-pound allowance per man, so anxious was he to keep weights down, but some personal belongings could fairly be regarded as indispensable: the journey might be a long one, and there might be a winter in improvised quarters on an inhospitable coast at the other end. In his words, "A man under such conditions needs something to occupy his thoughts, some tangible memento of his home and people beyond the seas." The fly-leaf was torn out, and the passage does not say what became of it. The author's understanding is that the limit screened for more than weight: on the ice the gold coins could buy nothing, while the photographs could bring home to mind.

issues.problem: 稿件把“立刻出发”写成无条件的原计划。证据显示，这只是按期登陆前提下的安排；原文还写了备选方案：登陆太晚就越冬、布置补给站，到1915年尽早出发。中英文都截去了这个条件。

issues.proposed: zh 改为：原计划要宏大得多：若能按时登陆，横穿队伍就立刻出发，走1800英里，希望五个月内穿越极点、抵达罗斯海基地；若登陆太晚，就先越冬、布置补给站，1915年尽早出发。en 同步补上 "Should the landing be made too late in the season..." 这一备选。

evidence.quote: We had been on the march for seven days
